Article text:
LLMs are terrible at designing AI systems
LLMs don’t know how to design software that uses LLMs. They’re comfortable writing normal programs, but if you throw an AI-shaped problem at them, they will usually screw it up. Why is that?
Going down the symbolic rabbit hole
For example, this post describes an attempt to vibe-code a memory tool that would flag when one memory contradicted another 1 . This is a great instance of a task that was virtually impossible five years ago but is now relatively trivial due to LLMs. You can simply task a LLM with scanning for contradictions, either in a big batch or pairwise 2 .

Nov 16, 2026

Apache TVM Community
Recent work on agent-driven kernel generation and systems optimization has shown that coding agents can take on substantial systems development. With agents writing a growing share of systems code, validating its correctness has become an increasingly important problem. As we discussed in our recent post “Rethinking Abstractions in the Agentic Era” , ML compiler foundation will continue to play a central role in the agentic era, to inspect, verify, and transform the programs that agents generate.

Title: Show HN: Backplane – An AI Development Environment for Hardware
Article title: Backplane
Description: A TOTALLY open-source workspace for agentic hardware development.
HN text: We made Backplane to actually use Fable, Astra, etc. as real electrical engineers! It incorporates KiCad + your favorite harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok) to accelerate hardware development. You can use it "autonomously" or work alongside the agent, making changes or comments to redirect the agent as it works. Also has some slick skills for schematic editing, BOM management. Hardware is in its "tab to accept changes"/copilot era rather than its agentic era imo.
